title: Massive Attack Duo Banned From Singapore Over Palestinian Flag Display
full_text: Aug 1, 2026 2:26am PT Massive Attack Duo Banned From Singapore Over Palestinian Flag Display By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Massive Attack Duo Banned From Singapore Over Palestinian Flag Display 1 hour ago Oscar-Qualifying Bengaluru International Short Film Festival Expands to 10 Arenas, Adds AI and Dance Competitions (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago ‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’ Celebrates 10 Years as Longest-Running Two-Part Play in Modern West End History – Global Bulletin 2 days ago See All Getty Images Both members of Massive Attack have been permanently barred from re-entering Singapore after unfurling a Palestinian flag during the British trip-hop group’s concert in the city-state, according to a joint statement from the Singapore Police Force and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA). The statement said police investigated both band members for “their actions of support for a political cause and unfurling of a foreign flag” during the show at The Star Theatre on July 29. Following the investigation, and in consultation with the Attorney-General’s Chambers, police administered stern warnings to both men for offences under Section 3 of the Foreign National Emblems (Control of Display) Act 1949 and Section 16 of the Public Order Act. Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House “Both men will also be banned from re-entering Singapore,” the statement said. Popular on Variety According to the statement, the event organizer had acknowledged the licensing conditions attached to the concert beforehand, but both band members held up a “foreign flag” onstage during the performance, with one shouting “Free Palestine.” The IMDA said it is investigating a possible breach of several licence conditions, including one barring performers from displaying flags tied to any cause, and will act once that inquiry concludes. The regulator added it will not approve any future application for the band to perform in Singapore given the entry ban. The concert was the band’s only scheduled Singapore date on its current tour, with video of the flag display circulating widely online alongside footage of the crowd joining in chants of “Free Palestine.” The two men are Massive Attack’s founding members, Robert “3D” Del Naja and Grant “Daddy G” Marshall, who make up its current touring lineup; authorities did not name them in the statement. Singapore maintains strict rules on the public display of foreign flags and emblems without a permit, framing the laws as necessary to protect the country’s racial and religious harmony. The joint statement reiterated that position, with authorities saying they “take a serious view of acts which could potentially harm the racial and religious harmony in Singapore” and urging the public, including foreigners, “to refrain from importing foreign politics” into the country. “The peace and harmony between different races and religions in Singapore should not be taken for granted, and we must not let external events affect our society,” the statement said. Massive Attack has been among the more vocal acts in music in its support for Palestinian causes. Del Naja was arrested earlier this year during a demonstration in London tied to Palestine Action, a group proscribed in the U.K. Variety has reached out to Massive Attack’s representation for comment. ‘Chimney Town: Frozen in Time’ Sells Wide Across Europe Ahead of Annecy French Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) Berlinale Title ‘Members of the Problematic Family’ to Open Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... title: ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie in the Works at Netflix With Original Lead Cast to Return
full_text: Aug 1, 2026 2:17am PT ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie in the Works at Netflix With Original Lead Cast to Return By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie in the Works at Netflix With Original Lead Cast to Return 1 hour ago ‘The Odyssey’ Craze Continues as New BFI Imax Screenings Sell Out in Under 30 Minutes (EXCLUSIVE) 19 hours ago Irish Indie Film ‘Lemonade,’ Starring Barry Keoghan, Reveals First Images and Plot Details (EXCLUSIVE) 21 hours ago See All Everett Collection “ The Inbetweeners ” — the hit Brit teen comedy series from the late 2000s that spawned two successful spin-off films — is officially back. A reunion movie is now in the works at Netflix , Variety has confirmed, with the original lead cast of Simon Bird, Joe Thomas, Blake Harrison and James Buckley understood to be attached, although final deals are yet to be finalized. The news comes less than a year after rights holders Banijay U.K. revealed that it had struck a deal with “The Inbetweeners” creators Iain Morris and Damon Beesley and their Fudge Park Productions that, at the time, they said “paves the way for the return of the hit comedy title.” But it was then unknown in what shape or form — and on what platform — that return would look like. Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Netflix, it seems, has fallen for the show’s famed foul-mouthed library of hilariously puerile quotes. Popular on Variety Originally broadcast on E4 in the U.K. between 2008 and 2010, “The Inbetweeners” follows the misadventures of suburban teenager Will MacKenzie (Bird) and his friends Simon Cooper (Thomas), Neil Sutherland (Harrison) and Jay Cartwright (Buckley) at the fictional Rudge Park Comprehensive as they navigated school life, friendship, male bonding, lad culture and failed sexual encounters. It was originally conceived as a more realistic counterpoint to fellow hit Brit teen show “Skins,” showcasing an adolescence that is awkward and — as Morris suggested at the time — mostly “crap.” After three seasons, two hit movies followed, released in 2011 and 2014 respectively. The first set a record for the biggest opening weekend for a U.K. comedy at the time of its release with the sequel also breaking box office records. “Incredibly exciting to be plotting more adventures for our four favourite friends (ooh friends),” Morris and Beesley said after the news that “The Inbetweeners” would return in 2025. title: FIFA Chief Gianni Infantino on the Ropes as He Ditches Controversial $20 Billion Private Investment Plan
full_text: Jul 31, 2026 11:41pm PT FIFA Chief Gianni Infantino on the Ropes as He Ditches Controversial $20 Billion Private Investment Plan By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest FIFA Chief Gianni Infantino on the Ropes as He Ditches Controversial $20 Billion Private Investment Plan 4 hours ago Gary Oldman, ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker and ‘Barbie’ Producer Robbie Brenner Among Toronto Market Speakers 23 hours ago World Cup Boycott Backed by All 55 UEFA Countries as Asian, North and Central American, Caribbean Members Oppose FIFA Stake Sale 1 day ago See All Courtesy of Getty Gianni Infantino , the embattled president of soccer’s governing body FIFA , has abandoned his controversial plan to create a $20 billion company, FIFA Forward Enterprise, that would control the commercial rights to its events, principally the World Cup. In a statement released late Friday, Infantino said it had “become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.” Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House The survival of Infantino, who is up for re-election for a fourth term as president at the FIFA Congress in March, is now in doubt. Popular on Variety Infantino said, “Our purpose has always been – and will always be – to unite and improve. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game.” The climbdown by Infantino follows a threat by European countries, represented by the continent’s soccer governing body UEFA, to boycott all FIFA events, including the World Cup, if the plan moved forward. Opposition to Infantino’s plan had also come from Concacaf, which governs soccer in North, Central America and the Caribbean, and the sport’s governing body in Asia, the Asian Football Confederation. Resistance to the plan had also come from within FIFA. Carlos Cordeiro, Infantino’s senior adviser on global strategy and governance, resigned over the issue, saying the proposal was “a bad deal” for soccer and would “mortgage” its future. Then on Friday, the organization’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said its own administration had been “deceived” about the project. Lamour described the plan as “the project of one person,” and said, “the time has now come for [soccer’s] political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.” Lamour added that he had a duty of loyalty to “certain values” and supporting his colleagues. “If that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.” Under Infantino’s proposal, each FIFA member country would have received an initial payment of $20 million and a doubling of their annual stipend to $5 million. This would have been partially funded by the sale of a roughly 20% stake in FIFA Forward Enterprise to an investor group led by Thrive Eternal. Thrive Eternal is run by Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared Kushner is married to President Donald Trump’s daughter Ivanka. title: ‘Barbie’ Sequel Stalled as Warner Bros. Tries to Reach Deals With Greta Gerwig, Margot Robbie, Ryan Gosling
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All July 31, 2026 8:03pm Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling in 'Barbie' Courtesy of Warner Bros. Entertainment The Barbie sequel has hit a roadblock on its way back to Barbieland. Warner Bros. has until December to reach a deal with the stars of the 2023 film, Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling , as well as director and co-writer Greta Gerwig , before the rights revert to Mattel, according to a report from the New York Times . The studio has been negotiating with the principal talent for months, offering them a share of the profits if the film reaches certain box office milestones. The outlet also claims that Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav declined to approve the proposed deal because he believed it was “too generous.” Related Stories Movies Gary Oldman, Curry Barker, 'Barbie' Producer Robbie Brenner to Keynote Toronto Film Festival Lifestyle Mattel's Collectible 2026 Barbie Holiday Doll Channels Festive Representation in Red The Times went on to report that a Warner Bros. spokesperson disputed that characterization, saying talent representatives declined an offer made in May and have not yet submitted a counteroffer. “We have a rights deal with Mattel in place and have made a series of big offers to try and finalize deals to make the next Barbie film,” studio co-chairs Pam Abdy and Michael De Luca said in a statement. “Unfortunately, we have been unable to reach an agreement thus far.” The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Warner Bros. for comment, and they had nothing further to add. Gerwig and her Barbie co-writer Noah Baumbach have had an idea for Barbie 2 for a couple of years. THR first reported in 2024 that the couple was in the “early stages” of developing a story for the sequel. Barbie was a massive hit with audiences and critics, grossing $1.5 billion worldwide and earning eight Oscar nominations, winning one for best original song (“What Was I Made For?” by Billie Eilish and Finneas O’Connell). Upon its release in July 2023, the film also became a cultural phenomenon thanks to its marketing campaign, signature pink aesthetic and simultaneous release with Christopher Nolan’s Oppenheimer , dubbing the name, “Barbenheimer.” THR

title: How Jack Haven Found “Innocence” in ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’ Slasher Little Death
full_text: × Skip to main content Jack Haven. Courtesy It might seem a bit jarring to hear that an actor “took a sweetness” from a character called Little Death, but Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma ’s Jack Haven found an innocence to the slasher in Jane Schoenbrun ’s latest feature. “It’s someone who isn’t killing because of a wicked and cruel instinct, but sort of just because of inevitability and curiosity,” the 31-year-old tells The Hollywood Reporter . In Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Misasma , a young filmmaker, played by Hannah Einbinder , is preparing to reboot a slasher franchise, Camp Miasma, which found Haven’s Little Death terrorizing and killing teen campers. Add the ultimate final girl, played by Gillian Anderson , and it’s an unbeatable formula. Related Stories Movies With 'Camp Miasma,' Hannah Einbinder Is Back in Another Complicated Cross-Generational Relationship Movies Karlovy Vary Fest Adds Cannes Winner 'Fjord' and 'Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma' “I like a character that just doesn’t quite know how human things work, but is interested in playing with them,” Haven explains. “[There’s] an innocence and a total inability to control the people around them in a manipulative way. This character has a deep power that’s a deep centered power, but has no interest in the social dynamics.” The actor gained recognition for their role in Netflix’s Atypical , along with roles in films like Bill and Ted Face the Music . They’ve also waded into the filmmaking waters in recent years. In Camp Miasma , Haven reunites with Schoenbrun after the pair worked together on the director’s acclaimed feature I Saw the TV Glow. “Jane is one of those rare and sacred collaborations that I just feel it’s intergalactic when I get to work with them,” Haven says. “I feel a great freedom when I’m with Jane,” they continue. “When I’m talking to Jane about creating something because they have a really unlimited imagination and they can travel through dimensions.” The actor says they’ll always work with Schoenbrun when the opportunity’s presented. Adds Haven, “I pack myself and I’m ready at the door.” Below, Haven digs into the film premiering at Cannes, working as a filmmaker and the Camp Miasma sequence that the actor found to be their most physically challenging scene ever. What drew you into the movie? I would’ve said yes to anything that Jane asked me to do, but they described the character as the slasher killer in a helmet with a slobbering tongue, and I was totally in. What was the Cannes experience like? I wish I was mentally stable enough to enjoy something like Cannes, but unfortunately I’m not. The best part was that I knew it was a good thing in my mind. Probably in my body, I knew it was a good thing. My mind turned invasive species mode and was running through the rainforest, trying not to get caught. It’s like, you know that scene in The Beach when Leonardo DiCaprio goes into video game mode and he’s being chased? It’s like that level of paranoia for some reason is elicited by environments in which capitalism and film are making out. I just, something about it, I run. But seeing everyone’s hard work, this beautiful group of people with the purest souls on earth being celebrated in this way was just magnificent. Also, my mom came, and it was really special to be there with her because she’s a longtime artist. It was just amazing to see it through her eyes. How do you work through getting over that in your own head? I’ve just been working on transcending it. It’s totally an ego thing because it’s like, first of all, no one really gives a shit about anyone else. At the core of every interaction is pure love, and we know that celebrity culture is done. I think it’s hilarious that we’re still dealing with these dynamics because we know they’re not real. Seeing a movie like Camp Miasma at Cannes, people just enter this state of bliss because they are in the imaginary dimension, even if just for a moment. For some reason, that’s what we like to pay for. We like to pay for things that glitter like the imaginary, like magic. This is the way our world is built right now, it won’t always be built like this and it hasn’t always been built like this, but that’s the mental gymnastics I have to do, which honestly should be quite easy because as I said, it’s all love. You recently did your first feature as a director, right? Can you tell me a bit about what that process of transitioning to filmmaking has been like? Yes, I have two features actually, but only one is available to see. The first one I made on my iPhone, and it was really because one of my close friends, Peter, he’s 73 and he had liver cancer, so he was dying. He’s the star of the film, so I wanted to make it as quickly as possible. He got the liver transplant halfway through and he survived, and so we finished the film with him. The second film, my good friend Clyde gave me money to buy a better camera. I wrote a script for that one. The first one was improvised, and that one was more produced. Then editing it is obviously hell. My best friend Mina Walker scored the movie. We’ve just finished that one. Now, I’m writing the third one. We’re going to shoot in August and September, [and it’s] is a comedy. I believe Jane said in the director’s notes that the one shot killing spree scene was the most proud they’ve been about anything they’d made. I’d really love to hear about that scene in particular. Jane had a shot by shot with them as Little Death. It [was] made at the camp before we started shooting. It was just an iPhone edit, which I hope gets released someday. But I can’t take really any credit for it. I know what my body is doing, and it’s like 3 a.m., and I do what I must do. The hardest part was probably the camera that was strapped to me. What was that like? I read it was very heavy. I don’t even know how heavy it was, but it felt like it was as heavy at least as me. It felt like the shadow self, honestly. It was balancing that. But the camera assistant, Emma, was holding the camera, and then there were sandbags on the back so it was counterbalanced, but it’s still… The fight choreographer, stunt choreographer, Maja Aro, had this really particular movement that we practiced so much, so I knew what I was doing. The pieces were all there, but it’s still probably the hardest thing I’ve had to do as an actor, just in terms of physical intensity. The stunt people in the background, they were doing such hard work because they were throwing themselves against the wall and then falling to the rhythm of the stabs. We did it maybe eight times, and still on the last take, I screamed afterwards because I forgot something. But I guess we got it. What did you feel like seeing the scene? Totally blown away. As with the whole film, as with all of Jane’s work. Even when Jane describes something or describes an idea for a film, that’s unlike anything. It really feels like a feeling of your grandmother telling you a story as a child, it’s that wonder. THR

title: All of the Guest Stars and Cameos on HBO Max’s ‘Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness’ (So Far)
full_text: Skip to main content By Kevin Dolak Plus Icon Kevin Dolak View All July 31, 2026 6:53pm Ike Barinholtz as Henry Ford and Larry David as a rabbi in Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness' Photograph by John Johnson/HBO Logo text Larry David has returned to HBO Max with the American history-centered sketch comedy show Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness , following the conclusion of his long-running series Curb Your Enthusiasm — and it’s not just executive producers Barack and Michelle Obama who are along for the ride. Dozens of celebrity guests have joined the comedian to fill out the cast of historical figures. This is not just a few cameos here and there — each episode of Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness has over a dozen celebrity guests, and the roster ranges from a few of David’s co-stars on Curb to the late Rob Reiner , in what became his final screen performance. Major Hollywood stars including Samuel L. Jackson and Lin-Manuel Miranda don the wigs and garb of decades and centuries past alongside television’s biggest names, like Jerry Seinfeld and Jon Hamm. The Hollywood Reporter is watching the series closely to make sure all these stars are accounted for — after all, they deserve some credit for spending time working with L.D. Related Stories TV HBO Max Picks Up 'Friday the 13th' Prequel Series 'Crystal Lake' Across Europe Music Barack Obama Puts Glen Hansard, SZA, Drake, Beatles on His Songs of the Summer Playlist New episodes of Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness air Friday nights at 9 p.m. on HBO and stream on HBO Max. Episode 1 – “Livingston” President Barack Obama as Himself; Samuel L. Jackson as The Narrator; Henry Winkler as John Hancock; Chris Parnell as Benjamin Franklin; Alan Tudyk as Thomas Jefferson; Alison Becker as Spectator 1; Mary Sohn as Spectator 2; Rodney J. Hobbs as Spectator 3; Richard Kind as Thomas Watson; Jake Reiner as Private Wallace; Mike Castle as Private Smith; Michael Chiklis as Sergeant; and Jurnee Smollett as Rosa Parks. The series opens with an appearance by one of its EPs and a familiar face to all: former President Barack Obama, whose Higher Ground Productions is behind the historical sketch comedy show. Obama praises the nation he led for eight years as it reaches its semiquincentennial and dunks on David a bit — because why not? He’s America’s most beloved curmudgeon. The intro gives way to narration from Samuel L. Jackson, a go-to voiceover these days, giving Morgan Freeman a run for his money. The first sketch has Winkler, Parnell and Tudyk as our founding fathers as they shut down the additions David’s Robert Livingston is trying to include in the grievances section of the Declaration of Independence. Next up, David portrays Alexander Graham Bell, forced to make awkward conversation with Curb cast member and national treasure Kind as Thomas Watson, as Bell debuts the telephone to a crowd of revelers already demanding text messaging and a variety of color options for the new invention. The annoying crowd features sitcom stalwarts Alison Becker ( Parks and Recreation ), Mary Sohn ( A.P. Bio ) and Rodney J. Hobbs ( The Office , Modern Family ). The third sketch involves WWI trench warfare, where David portrays a cowardly soldier under the command of a sergeant, played by none other than The Shield ‘s Michael Chiklis; his fellow soldiers are Comedy Bang Bang and Curb alum Mike Castle and Jake Reiner, the son of the late Rob Reiner (who also appeared on Curb ). The premiere episode closes with David as an irritating bus passenger who sits next to famed civil rights icon Rosa Parks, perfectly cast with Jurnee Smollett in the role. Episode 2 – “Farewell” Samuel L. Jackson as The Narrator; Rita Wilson as Mavis Lewis; Jerry Seinfeld as William Clark; Matthew Jones as Tilden’s Aide; Rich Fulcher as Tilden’s Aide; Larry Wilmore as Barney; Kaley Cuoco as Gloria, the Widow; Colton Dunn as Dominic the Soup Server; Rob Reiner as George Washington; Jimmy Kimmel as Crowd Member; and Allan Havey as Crowd Member. The second episode opens with a reunion between the two creators of the greatest sitcom of all time: Larry David and Jerry Seinfeld. The comedy duo behind the ’90s hit Seinfeld portrays explorers Lewis and Clark, whose landmark military mission, commissioned by President Thomas Jefferson, mapped the newly acquired Louisiana Territory and sought a water route to the Pacific Ocean. The gag is that the two are drinking buddies and it’s a bit too convenient they’re off to explore together for years on their own — as noted by Rita Wilson as Mavis Lewis, Meriwether Lewis’s long-suffering wife. David then skewers the Electoral College as he portrays Samuel Tilden, who won the popular vote in the 1876 presidential election but fell one vote shy of an Electoral College majority, ultimately losing to Rutherford B. Hayes. Ranting ensues as Matthew Jones, a Curb alum, and Rich Fulcher of The Mighty Boosh portray his aides. Next, in a Great Depression-set segment, David is joined by Larry Wilmore (formerly of late-night fame) and the incomparable Colton Dunn ( Superstore , Parks and Recreation ), and, in a series highlight, Kaley Cuoco as a grieving widow David is trying to use to cut in line for bread for his soup. Finally, the episode ends with the much-talked-about final screen appearance of Rob Reiner; here he portrays George Washington as he discusses term limits for the U.S. presidency in front of a gathered crowd. It’s all a setup for David’s townsman to take veiled swipes at President Trump, who is not named but we all know who L.D. is talking about. Jimmy Kimmel delightfully turns up in some meta-commentary on his forever feud with Trump, too. Episode 3 – “McCarthy” Samuel L. Jackson as The Narrator; Lou DiMaggio as Colonial Man; Lin-Manuel Miranda as Michael Finney; Jordan Black as Samuel Cooper; Brad Morris as Joseph Warren; J.B. Smoove as Jonesy Dean Sharpe; Armoire Tru Valentino as Ottoman Jon Hamm as Orville Wright; Sean Hayes as Wilbur Wright; Michael McKean as Joseph Welch; and Rob Huebel as Senator Mundt. The episode opens with David again playing his usual “guy caught up in a real historical moment” role as he crashes the Boston Tea Party [see flag No. 2 above]. Lin-Manuel Miranda, in fun stunt casting given his Broadway Revolutionary War pedigree from Hamilton , steals the scene as one of the Tea Party ringleaders. Comedian Lou DiMaggio appears too, playing off David’s character being left out of the rebellion. Speaking of scene stealers, J.B. Smoove’s character Jonesey makes a stop along the Underground Railroad, flabbergasting David’s host with his demands and, soon, his arriving friends. Next, David plays a fictional, less-than-heroic Wright sibling squabbling with his wife (Isla Fisher) over her critique of his butter-churning skills, while Jon Hamm and Sean Hayes play the actual Orville and Wilbur Wright preparing for the first flight. The episode’s closing and most talked-about segment features David himself playing Senator Joseph McCarthy. It also features SNL alum and Better Call Saul ‘s Michael McKean as attorney Joseph Welch, delivering the famous “Have you no decency, sir?” rebuttal, and Rob Huebel ( Human Giant , Transparent ) as a senator helping moderate one of the infamous hearings. Episode 4 – “Deepthroat” Samuel L. Jackson as The Narrator; Beck Bennett as Bob Woodward; Ike Barinholtz as Henry Ford; Diallo Riddle as John Appleton; Katie Aselton as Sylvia Jordana Brewster; Beatrice Merle Dandridge as Clementine; Andrea Savage as Cordelia; Rory Scovel as Jefferson Davis; Judy Gold as Evelyn; Adam Lustick as Jonas Salk; and Gregg “Jeep” Perrie as Bobby. The Watergate scandal gets the Larry David treatment: in the first sketch of the fourth episode, he portrays “Deep Throat,” the anonymous source who leaked details of the hotel break-in to Washington Post reporters. But David’s leaker doesn’t provide any useful information to SNL alum Beck Bennett’s Woodward when they meet in a parking lot — just trivial nonsense. Next up, Ike Barinholtz plays the notoriously antisemitic Henry Ford, less than thrilled to be showing his new vehicle to David’s rabbi character. David then portrays President James Buchanan, hitting on each passing lady at a party where he’s introduced the concept of passed appetizers in lieu of dinner. Jordana Brewster of the Fast & Furious movies and The Other Two , and The League ‘s Katie Aselton, are among the unfortunate ladies to cross his path; Diallo Riddle ( Marlon , South Side ) is Buchanan’s assistant, John Appleton. The big talker of the episode is saved for the finale, with David reviving an old stand-up bit as the overly proud mother of Jonas Salk, Dora, bragging on her son to her neighbor Evelyn about his discovery of the polio vaccine. It gets personal as David mocks his former friend and former co-star Cheryl Hines’ husband, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Soon a young man named Bobby turns up to naysay, telling Dora Salk, “That vaccine’s gonna kill people. It’s gonna give them heart attacks!” A parody of the stark politics of the MMR vaccine ensues, as only David could script. Episode 5 – “Lincoln” Samuel L. Jackson as The Narrator; Don Johnson as Doc Holiday; Timothy Olyphant as Wyatt Earp; Johnno Wilson as Virgil Earp; Marc Menchaca as Joseph Clanton; Maximo Salas as Young Clanton; Bill Hader as Abraham Lincoln; Kathryn Hahn as Mary Todd Lincoln; Lennon Parham as Laura Keene; Jay Renshaw as John Wilkes Booth; and Seth Morris as Andrew Johnson. Only two historical moments get the Larry David treatment in the fifth installment of the sketch series, but they are two pretty big moments. First, we’re at the O.K. Corral with Wyatt Earp (Timothy Olyphant) and Doc Holliday (Don Johnson), as a classic Curb -style obnoxious conversation about logistics gets applied to the location and timing of the famous shootout on Oct. 26, 1881. Marc Menchaca ( Curb ‘s Klansman Joe) plays a cowboy who calls out L.D.’s “pig-parking” job; Johnno Wilson as Virgil Earp and Maximo Salas as Young Clanton round out the cast of outlaws. Abraham Lincoln’s strained relationship with his wife, Mary Todd Lincoln, became Broadway fodder recently with Cole Escola’s Tony Award-winning turn in Oh, Mary! , and now it’s David’s turn to give us his take on the mentally unstable first lady. Bill Hader of SNL and Barry gives us a put-upon Lincoln who, in the sketch, connives with his chief of staff, Lawrence Butterfield, to get rid of Mary at Ford’s Theatre. A game of telephone ensues, with Lincoln wedged between the two as they watch Our American Cousin from box seats. The sketch’s second half has Butterfield and Mary arguing over a stolen sweater in another moment that could be straight out of Curb . Episode 6 Samuel L. Jackson as The Narrator; Essence Atkins as Clara; Susie Essman as Susan B. Anthony; Wayne Federman as Alfred; Isla Fisher as Elsbeth; Toby Huss as Herbert; Keegan-Michael Key as Davy Crockett; Jane Krakowski as Edith; Kyle Mooney as Paul Revere; Oscar Nunez as General Santa Anna; Marques Ray as Army Scout and Paul Rudd as Neil Armstrong. By episode six, Larry David and Jeff Schaffer have given some memorable and some quite obscure moments in American history the Curb Your Enthusiasm treatment, but they most certainly have not run out of significant events to lampoon or significant figures to torture. Spanning from before the American Revolution to the 1969 Apollo 11 mission, the sixth installment opens with Paul Revere’s historic ride and L.D. as a colonial resident and Isla Fisher as his wife at each other’s throats as the stress of the arrival of the hated British mounts. Next, we’re in the midst of the Texas Revolution with Keegan-Michael Key hamming it up as a doofus Davy Crockett, arguing with L.D. as he tries to get him to reveal his secret spot for defecation outside of the Alamo, arguing about the Crockett myth of killing a bear as a lad and demanding he reveal the bald head beneath his iconic raccoon cap. In the third sketch, that uncomfortable spark of magic between David and Susie Essman that made Curb such an uncomfortable delight is back. Now, Essman is suffragette Susan B. Anthony, who is throwing a booze-free dinner party that irks her most obnoxious guest, played by you-know-who, a longtime avatar for the rageful response to David’s antics. Essman shows here she’s still got it. The penultimate episode ends with the 1969 moon landing as Paul Rudd’s Neil Armstrong bickers and then dukes it out with David’s Buzz Aldrin. This story was originally published on July 17, and has been updated as new episodes release. THR

title: FIFA Boss Infantino Scraps World Cup Sell Off Plans After Backlash
full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All July 31, 2026 6:20pm President Gianni Infantino holds the FIFA World Cup winner's trophy. Sam Hodde/Getty Images After announcing plans earlier this week for FIFA to sell off a stake in the World Cup to private investors, the president of the global soccer governing body, Gianni Infantino , has announced he’s pulling those plans. “The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed. And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders,” Infantino said in a statement on Friday. Related Stories TV FIFA Boss Infantino Under Fire Over World Cup Sell Off Plans Business Opposition Grows to FIFA World Cup Sell-Off Plan “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” he continued. “Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.” The proposed plan would have consisted of FIFA setting up a new entity, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), that would bundle soccer associated money-making operations while a significant stake would be sold to private investors. 20 percent of the company would have been sold to Thrive Capital, an invest group run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Backlash was immediate, with European soccer body UEFA saying on Thursday that if the plan went through, it would boycott FIFA events , including the World Cup . Three of the four semi-finalists of the 2026 men’s World Cup hailed from Europe, including this year’s champion, Spain . Earlier this week, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham released a statement online that read, “football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine. The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.” Infantino’s statement continued, “Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.” THR

title: FIFA Scraps Controversial Plan To Turn World Cup Into Commercial Enterprise
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Patrick Hipes Patrick Hipes Executive Managing Editor More Stories By Patrick Tournament Of Roses Organization And Its Rose Parade Sign With UTA Movie Academy Re-Elects Lynette Howell Taylor As President Michael J. Fox To Receive TV Academy’s Bob Hope Humanitarian Award At This Year’s Emmys View All July 31, 2026 6:20pm FIFA president Gianni Infantino Getty Images FIFA on Friday said it would not move forward with a plan to create a $20 billion commercial arm of soccer’s world governing body by selling stakes in the World Cup and other events to private investors. The proposal had been met by a wave of criticism by several soccer confederations from the time it was proposed just days ago, with major groups repping Europe, Asia and the Americas condemning the plan that would have radically restructured the global non-profit organization. Related Stories Sports FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal News Donald Trump, As Expected, Awarded New FIFA Peace Prize At World Cup Draw “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in a statement released Friday evening. “Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.” Watch on Deadline Statement attributable to the FIFA President The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed. And more so, as we said… — FIFA Media (@fifamedia) July 31, 2026 The plan, which Infantino announced Tuesday and contingent on a member vote, came on the heels of the summer’s wildly profitable 2026 FIFA World Cup hosted by the U.S., Mexico and Canada. The proposal would have created a commercial arm called FIFA Forward Enterprise, which was being valued at $20 billion. FFE would operate the commercial side of the sport as a dedicated business, with profits shared with member associations like UEFA (Europe), CONCACAF (the Americas, which includes the U.S.) and Asia (the AFC). The World Cup is not a commercial enterprise, but FFE would allow it to be exploited by private investors. FIFA had said it would be the controlling shareholder, but that it had hoped to raise $4.2 billion by “carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests.” Thrive Capital, an investment firm led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, was among the investors approached, per reports. Reactions to commercializing the men’s and women’s World Cups and other major tournaments like the Club World Cup were swift. UEFA — home to World Cup winner Spain as well as semifinalists England and France and six of the eight quarterfinalists — said all 55 of its member states will boycott the World Cup if FIFA enacted the plan to sell stakes in the tournament to private investors. “The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies,” it wrote after its membership voted in an emergency meeting Thursday. “It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.” CONCACAF and its 41 members also formally opposed the plan Thursday, questioning “the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history.” The AFC joined in opposition earlier today. The number of countries in the three federations is more than 140, well above the majority needed to reject the plan required ratification. “The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed,” FIFA said in its statement tonight. “And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.” It added: “Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.” The next major tournament on the FIFA schedule is the 2027 Women’s World Cup next summer in Brazil. The next men’s World Cup is in 2030 co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco. title: Javier Bardem Politely Warned ‘Cape Fear’ Co-Star About Grabbing Her Hair During Attack Scene and Apologized in Advance: ‘I’m So Sorry, My Love’
full_text: Jul 31, 2026 6:00pm PT Javier Bardem Politely Warned ‘Cape Fear’ Co-Star About Grabbing Her Hair During Attack Scene and Apologized in Advance: ‘I’m So Sorry, My Love’ By Antonio Ferme Plus Icon Antonio Ferme Latest ‘Obsession’ Star Inde Navarrette Confirms Meeting With ‘X-Men’ Director Jake Schreier and Would Love to Play Mystique 18 hours ago ‘The Odyssey’: What Academics Are Saying About Christopher Nolan’s Epic 2 weeks ago Why Aren’t There More Imax 70mm Screens for ‘The Odyssey’? ‘It’s Not Practical,’ Company Says 2 weeks ago See All Getty Images In 2007, Javier Bardem delivered one of the century’s most chilling performances as Anton Chigurh in “No Country for Old Men.” Nearly two decades later, he’s proved once again he could convincingly play a sociopath, reimagining the vengeful murderer Max Cady on Apple TV +’s hit summer series “ Cape Fear .” Cady was previously played by Robert Mitchum in 1962 and Robert De Niro in 1991, but the brilliance of Bardem’s performance lies in the long stretches of perceived stillness, heightening the tension of the cat-and-mouse game he plays with the Bowden family, which star Lily Collias described as “a lot of fun” but “sometimes very jarring.” “We’re playing cat and mouse, and then the cameras turn off, and I still feel like a mouse,” Collias told Variety at the “Cape Fear” finale screening in New York. “And he still feels like Tom from ‘Tom and Jerry.’” Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Collias plays Natalie Bowden, the daughter of Anna (Amy Adams) and Tom (Patrick Wilson), two lawyers who Bardem’s Cady blames for his incarceration. After 10 episodes of buildup, the series finale depicts an epic battle in which Cady invades the Bowden’s home, placing Anna and Tom on “trial” for colluding against him and threatening their children. Popular on Variety “[Episode] 10 felt almost like a play,” Collias said. “It was just the family and him in the house, and we were doing the most insane things and laughing so hard off camera. title: John Galliano to Take Spotlight at Met Gala and Costume Institute Exhibition 16 Years After Antisemitic Rant
full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All July 31, 2026 5:28pm John Galliano attends Vogue's Forces of Fashion Conference at Milk Studios in New York on Oct. 12, 2017. (Photo by Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images) It’s official: John Galliano has been selected for a career-spanning exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 2027. The move to give Galliano’s work a coveted spotlight in the Met’s Costume Institute — an exhibition that serves as the centerpiece for the annual Met Gala , one of the world’s most watched and obsessed-over red carpet events — makes him the third living designer to receive a solo exhibition at the Met. The honor was previously bestowed upon Yves Saint Laurent (in 1983) and Rei Kawakubo (in 2017). Related Stories Lifestyle Disney and Old Navy Team Up for New Haunted Halloween Line of Cozy Flannels, PJs and Totes Lifestyle Womenswear Designer Rosie Assoulin Teams With Target to Deliver Luxury for Less That means his entire career, from runway highs to antisemitic lows, will fall into focus at the Met. It will cover the start at his namesake label before he segued to culture-shifting work at Givenchy and later, Dior, where he led the famed house for nearly 15 years as creative director from October 1996 through March 2011. More recently, he has led Maison Margiela from 2014 through 2024. And it will not shy away from his firing by Dior when video footage surfaced showing an inebriated Galliano making antisemitic remarks in a Paris café. The tirade not only led to a professional downfall and a retreat from public life for approximately two years, Galliano was found guilty by a Paris court of public insults based on religion, race, and ethnicity. He received a fine and was forced to pay damages and court fees. Galliano’s retreat, well-detailed in reports, interviews and a documentary, included meeting with Jewish leaders, rabbis and receiving blessings from groups like the Anti-Defamation League. Per today’s news — as detailed in a press release and an exclusive report from The New York Times’ Vanessa Friedman — the Met’s exhibition is not meant to present “a conventional narrative of disgrace and redemption” but rather “how aesthetic achievement, ethical accountability and institutional recognition intersect.” In addition to his accountability for the drunken tirade, Galliano has also said recovery has been key to this new chapter of his life after alcoholism and drug addiction caused turmoil in the previous era. “John Galliano has exerted a profound influence on fashion over the past four decades,” offered Max Hollein, The Met’s Marina Kellen French director and CEO, in a statement. “His work brings historical inquiry, artistic imagination, theatrical expression and technical experimentation into dynamic relation. Drawing upon the depth of The Costume Institute’s scholarship and the breadth of The Met’s collections, ‘John Galliano: Horizons’ will offer an expansive examination of his creative practice while attending closely to the historical, cultural and ethical circumstances through which his work is understood.” Per NYT ‘s Friedman, the decision did not come easily or expeditiously. She reports that Galliano, Met Costume Institute curator Andrew Bolton, Vogue global editorial director Anna Wintour (a longtime Galliano champion), and a “handful of influential rabbis and Jewish leaders in New York City” met for a closed-door meeting in May to discuss the possibility of a Galliano exhibit. Friedman reported that it was “one of several such meetings” held with Jewish leaders over the past year. According to a press release, Galliano’s exhibit will be divided into three sections, “Bearings,” “Horizons” and “Atlas of Transformation.” It will be accompanied by a catalog penned by Bolton, published by The Met and distributed internationally by Yale University Press. “Every Galliano collection begins as a journey among things separated by time, place, or medium: portrait and posture, silhouette and story, memory and material,” per Bolton in a press release. “‘Horizons’ approaches fashion as a form of cartography, mapping not territories but affinities, tensions, and transformations. It traces how images become ideas, ideas become material, and material becomes emotion. Yet a horizon reveals not only what lies before us, but also where we stand. The exhibition therefore considers both how Galliano has remapped the world through fashion and how his conduct, its consequences, and changing cultural values have reshaped our understanding of his work.” Galliano is now designing for Zara under a two-year deal to “re-author the brand’s archive” by “deconstructing and reconfiguring them into new seasonal expressions and creations.” His first collection is expected in September. full_text: Jul 31, 2026 4:47pm PT ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Leaks Online: Millions Watched Bootleg Before It Was Taken Down By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Leaks Online: Millions Watched Bootleg Before It Was Taken Down 10 hours ago ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Director Breaks Down His Bloody, One-Location Shark Movie, Those ‘Demanding’ Stunts and Why Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor Wanted to Switch Roles 11 hours ago ‘Big Brother 28’ Contestant Jason Breaks Down That Explosive Tea Party and Not Letting Kamu ‘Bully’ Him: ‘Isn’t It Interesting How the Six People in Power Were So Threatened by a Drag Queen?’ 15 hours ago See All ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection While Marvel fans are expected to turn out in droves to see “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ” in theaters this weekend, a high-quality bootleg of the film leaked on X, with millions of people having viewed it. Posted by an account named Fredrick Bryan at 6:05 a.m. PT, the leaked video reached 5.9 million accounts and counting, with over 143,000 people liking the post and 10,000 people resharing before it was taken down around 3:25 p.m. PT. Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Several other X accounts also posted copies, though most didn’t last long on the platform. Studios typically send infringement notices to those posting unauthorized copies, though it can be difficult to keep ahead of the volume of posting for the most popular new films. Popular on Variety Sony had no comment. “Brand New Day” is far from the first big-budget film to leak online. Last week, Christopher Nolan’s tentpole “The Odyssey” leaked on X with its own high-quality bootleg. title: Juliette Lewis On If ‘Cape Fear’s Crystal Or Max Is “More Psychopathic,” Martin Scorsese’s Lasting Support & Season 2 Hopes: “We Will See”
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Home Improvement’s Patricia Richardson Reunites With TV Sons Jonathan Taylor Thomas, Taran Noah Smith: “My Other Boys” ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Is X’s Latest Bootleg Leak, Gets Millions Of Views Before Taken Down Lorde Pauses Lollapalooza Show As Multiple Fans Pass Out View All July 31, 2026 4:25pm Juliette Lewis as Crystal Cady in Apple TV's 'Cape Fear' Apple TV SPOILERS: This post contains details about the Cape Fear , Season 1 finale episode “The Executioners” With another twisty-turny ride down Cape Fear reaching an end, Juliette Lewis was thrilled to have a chance to return to an important title from her youth, from a new perspective. The Oscar-nominated actress, who plays convicted killer Max Cady’s (Javier Bardem) sister Crystal in the Apple TV series, praised series creator Nick Antosca for giving her “so much to play” as a mentally disturbed figure from the sociopathic character’s past. The role comes 35 years after her breakout performance as public defender Sam Bowden’s (Nick Nolte) daughter Danielle in the Martin Scorsese -helmed 1991 feature adaptation of John D. MacDonald’s 1957 novel The Executioners . “But that was what was exciting, is that me coming back would be in a character that goes toe-to-toe with Max Cady, with our new Max Cady, and that they have this deep history, where you don’t know who the lion is and who the mouse is at any given time,” Lewis told Deadline. “And that she really gets under his skin and vice versa.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News ‘Cape Fear’ Series Creator “Always Wanted” Juliette Lewis To Star In Reboot News Juliette Lewis Makes Surprise ‘Cape Fear’ Cameo After Starring In 1991 Movie — Plus Francesca Scorsese Following their work together on Hulu’s 2019 limited series The Act , Antosca came to Lewis with a “three-page backstory” for the character of Crystal Cady, which Lewis said “was so rich with drama,” including the big twist revealed in Friday’s Season 1 finale episode “The Executioners”. After Max served 17 years for killing his pregnant wife Melissa, whose unborn baby was taken from the scene, his former attorney Anna Bowden (Amy Adams) learns the truth. Crystal (Lewis) escaped from the mental institution where she was committed, killing Melissa and taking the baby to raise as her own. Max Mattern as Luke and Juliette Lewis as Crystal Cady in Apple TV’s ‘Cape Fear’ “It’s so funny, because series work is a little bit different than film,” noted Lewis. “You often take a part, and you don’t know what’s coming, and they often don’t wanna tell you because they’re trying to keep these little nuggets secret from online and outward. But Nick, thank God, was such a good collaborator because he told me [from the beginning]. Lewis added, “I need to know because I like to create what it is I’m not showing, and I like to know where we’re going. And so, I knew all the things. I knew how savage she was from the very beginning, but of course I am who I am. I’m not gonna telegraph that. We wanna really make a real kind of psychopath. It’s like who’s more psychopathic, her or Max Cady? You decide.” And although the finale sees Max shoot Crystal and Luke (Max Mattern) and throw them into the hull of a burning boat, without realizing the young man is his own son, Lewis thinks a second season could provide another twist to that storyline. “Well, we will see. I hope to have a second season, because I know a little stuff about the second season,” teased Lewis. “But that’s what’s exciting about Nick, the show creator’s writing. It’s always twists and turns. It’s always to get you going in one direction as an audience and then, jaw-dropping. He really had fun creating that as a noir and a thriller. What’s behind this door? And it’s never what you expect.” Robert De Niro and Juliette Lewis in ‘Cape Fear’ (1991) (MCA/Courtesy Everett Collection) Following her Academy Award-nominated performance in the 1991 movie, which starred Robert De Niro as Max Cady, Lewis has found the experience “so meaningful” for bringing her back to Scorsese, who executive produces the series along with Steven Spielberg. “It’s a piece of my history and my career. It’s sort of my birthplace. It’s like my creative origin story is Cape Fear ,” said Lewis. “And then Scorsese, I consider one of my first and most important teachers. He validated me early on when I was an introvert and I had no articulation of my process, but I had a very strong point of view and instincts, and he knew early on to validate that and give me encouragement where I needed and so that I could be the adventurous, daring performer that I hope people think I am, but that I try to be. And making choices and not playing it safe, that’s because I had a Scorsese early on who gave me encouragement and gave me the floor. I kind of say metaphorically, he gave me the dance floor and the space to create. He didn’t damper these ideas.” Read on about Juliette Lewis’ return to Cape Fear , all episodes of which are now available to stream on Apple TV+ . DEADLINE: I really enjoyed the character of Crystal Cady and what she adds to the Cape Fear story that has been told multiple times now. JULIETTE LEWIS: Oh, thanks. DEADLINE: Tell me about how Nick [Antosca] approached you for the role and how it came full circle from your last time in Cape Fear . LEWIS: It was really amazing because I had worked with Nick [on Hulu’s The Act ]. We wanted to do something together. We had a general meeting and he pitched the idea … “I’m thinking about doing Cape Fear , but as a series. And I have some strong ideas about it.” And I was intrigued. That was pre-pandemic, I think 2019. It went away, and then I saw Amy Adams’ name and Javier Bardem attached. And because Hollywood can sometimes be a brutal place, I thought the ship had sailed without me. And so, I was like, “Oh gosh, should I reach out to Nick to say, hey, you remember the meeting we had, and you actually said you wanted me to be a part of it?” Anyway, two days later, he gave me an offer. He said, “No, I was keeping it a surprise. I was about to offer you this role.” And he had about a three-page backstory. The backstory was so rich with drama, and there was just so much to play. Even if you’re given a sentence, when you have such a strongly written backstory in a series, it makes the creation of a character really easy, because normally in series, you don’t. You just get one script and then some idea, but Nick is so thorough in his character development, and so that’s what’s exciting about working with him. But the short story is, I thought I wasn’t a part of it, and Nick had a part for me all along, and he kept his word. And he’s so smart, because I think people were really excited by my involvement. Juliette Lewis in Apple TV’s ‘Cape Fear’ (Hopper Stone/Apple TV+/Courtesy Everett Collection) DEADLINE: Tell me about reuniting with Martin Scorsese as the executive producer now. Did that bring up any memories from working on the movie? LEWIS: The whole thing is so meaningful for me because it’s a piece of my history and my career. It’s sort of my birthplace. It’s like my creative origin story is Cape Fear . When I became worldwide, people knew of me in this way on a global scale. You know, luck of the draw, I had no idea that that’s the impact it would have. And then Scorsese, I consider one of my first and most important teachers. He validated me early on when I was an introvert and I had no articulation of my process, but I had a very strong point of view and instincts, and he knew early on to validate that and give me encouragement where I needed and so that I could be the adventurous, daring performer that I hope people think I am, but that I try to be. And making choices and not playing it safe, that’s because I had a Scorsese early on who gave me encouragement and gave me the floor. I kind of say metaphorically, he gave me the dance floor and the space to create. He didn’t damper these ideas, because a lot of times early on, some people you work with, they just want a robot. And I was fortunate enough to work with the auteurs of American cinema who really validated my voice. And so, I always come to the table, trying to bring it something fully realized. But anyway, the short story is to say, gosh, it’s so important that that Scorsese gave it his blessing. I wasn’t on the table read, because I came in a few episodes later, but I’ll be seeing him shortly. I’ve seen him over the years. DEADLINE: Like you said, Crystal is just such a well fleshed-out character, and she’s really so fun to watch and kind of unsettling. Tell me about her dynamic with Max, that weird sibling dynamic and the effect she has over him. What it was like working with Javier on that? LEWIS: I’m so glad that reads. I haven’t seen the series, so I don’t know ever what edit they use and stuff. I’ve only heard about it, so people are telling me what we intended happened. But that was what was exciting, is that me coming back would be in a character that goes toe-to-toe with Max Cady, with our new Max Cady, and that they have this deep history, where you don’t know who the lion is and who the mouse is at any given time. And that she really gets under his skin and vice versa. And then also just on a pathology point, I was intrigued by playing a stalker, like stalker energy, obsession, obsessiveness—but they don’t know. They think they’re justified in everything they’re doing. She would never think she’s a stalker or somebody who’s obsessed. She’s just doing what she thinks is right and what is necessary. People don’t speak about acting this way, but I speak of it that it’s energy work, like I’m an energy worker, and what I mean by that is I’m conjuring energy. So that’s why some of my roles, I want people to feel it on a visceral level. But even when she comes in the first scene and she shows up at the bar where [Max] is sitting, and then they go in the cigar room, he brings her there. But even to show up, I wanted to have such a strong energy that’s so intimidating, but it’s veiled by, “I wouldn’t hurt anybody. I’m so sweet.” You know, sweetness and light. So, I love that dichotomy. I love the friction of the contradiction of what you show and what you conceal. It’s really exciting in character work for me. DEADLINE: Yeah, it was really fun to watch as well. Juliette Lewis in Apple TV’s ‘Cape Fear’ (2026) Apple TV LEWIS: But just to experience Javier as Max Cady—my first scene with him was when I saw him on the sidewalk, and I’m in the green coat. And He was just so exciting. He’s all the things. He’s all the things you want from a Max Cady, seductive, charismatic, dangerous and enticing. DEADLINE: Yeah, he’s always fun to watch as a bad guy, but he seems very sweet and charming in real life. LEWIS: Well, that’s the thing is, he really has a gift. Because I was in scenes, one inch apart, and when he puts that veil over his eyes, a veil of darkness, it’s something to behold. It’s really powerful, and so it was really exciting for me to work with him. We both respect each other so much, and we could just dance, metaphorically speaking. The couple scenes we have that are super intimate, almost face to face, just a half inch apart, it’s pretty electric. I hope it came off exciting. DEADLINE: Oh yeah, absolutely. It’s always twists and turns. It’s always to get you going in one direction as an audience and then, jaw dropping. He really had fun creating that as a noir and a thriller. What’s behind this door? And it’s never what you expect. LEWIS: Yeah, exactly. title: ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Director Breaks Down His Bloody, One-Location Shark Movie, Those ‘Demanding’ Stunts and Why Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor Wanted to Switch Roles
full_text: Jul 31, 2026 4:14pm PT ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Director Breaks Down His Bloody, One-Location Shark Movie, Those ‘Demanding’ Stunts and Why Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor Wanted to Switch Roles 'It's the hardest movie I've ever had to make,' director Jeff Wadlow says. By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Leaks Online: Millions Watched Bootleg Before It Was Taken Down 11 hours ago ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Director Breaks Down His Bloody, One-Location Shark Movie, Those ‘Demanding’ Stunts and Why Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor Wanted to Switch Roles 11 hours ago ‘Big Brother 28’ Contestant Jason Breaks Down That Explosive Tea Party and Not Letting Kamu ‘Bully’ Him: ‘Isn’t It Interesting How the Six People in Power Were So Threatened by a Drag Queen?’ 16 hours ago See All Courtesy of Amazon Studio When “The Devil’s Mouth” director Jeff Wadlow met the cast of his bloody shark movie, he made one thing clear. “‘Listen, this is going to be the most physically demanding job you’ve ever had. Not just because of the stunt work and all the underwater work, but the fact that when you have a simple dialogue scene, you’re going to be treading water,'” Wadlow recalls telling Kathryn Newton , Lana Condor and the rest of the ensemble. Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Written by Aja Gabel and Myung Joh Wesner, “The Devil’s Mouth” was named to the Black List back in 2019. Newton and Condor lead the cast as Sara and Max, two best friends whose friendship is tested after they get trapped in a freshwater cave — along with the rest of their college buddies, played by Gavin Casalegno, Tommi Rose and Nico Hiraga — while taking a trip to Thailand. Popular on Variety Of course, things get complicated when a bull shark enters the scene. In order to prep for the intensive shoot, the actors spent two weeks treading water, doing breath holds and training with real kayaks. Besides one stunt where Newton’s character had to hop off a 35-foot cliff into a shallow pool of water, all the actors were game to do their own stunts — safely, of course. “All the rock climbing, diving, underwater work, breath holds, getting dragged around on winches, that was all them,” Wadlow says. Known for helming lower-budget horror films for Blumhouse like “Imaginary,” “Fantasy Island” and “Truth or Dare,” Wadlow was first approached about directing the film during a meeting in which he was laser-focused on pitching his dream “G.I. Joe” trilogy. He had some hesitations when, instead, the words “shark movie” were mentioned. “I said, ‘I really don’t want to just do a shark movie unless there’s something new,'” Wadlow recalls. Then when he heard about the one-location aspect of the film, his creative juices began flowing, and he worked with Gabel and Wesner to rewrite the script. “Now we’re talking about an intersection between the shark movie genre and the claustrophobic horror movie,” he says. “I was blown away by how good it was because the character dynamics were complex and interesting. There’s a really nuanced investigation of female friendship.” Below, Wadlow breaks down casting Newton and Condor against usual type, how his team built 13 sets on two soundstages to pull off the illusion of an endless cave in Thailand, and why “The Devil’s Mouth” is “the hardest movie” he’s made to date. Talking about casting this friend group, what made Kathryn and Lana perfect for this central dynamic? What’s funny about casting this film is both Kathryn and Lana thought they should be playing the other part. And you can kind of see it! Having made the movie, I only see Kathryn as Sara, and I only see Lana as Max. But on the page, the characters were sort of similar to characters that they had played before. I ultimately think that made the movie so much more interesting because it forced Kathryn to stretch and grow and define a quieter character to play. She normally plays really out-there dynamic characters, and Sara’s got an internal journey; Lana usually plays like the good girl, this was a chance for her to play someone with a little more bite. They both really rose to the challenge and did it together. They became best friends while we were making the movie. We shot this whole thing in Thailand. Thailand is so far away from America that if you leave from the East Coast, you go through the Middle East, and if you leave from the West Coast, you go through Japan. It’s literally on the opposite side of the planet, and so there were no long weekends going home. Once we were there, we were all there, and it was a Thai movie. There were about less than a dozen Westerners working on it. How did you go about finding the cave? What were the biggest logistical challenges to filming inside? It’s the hardest movie I’ve ever had to make. I mean, in 85% of the movie, the characters are swimming in water. Movie cameras in water do not get along, as we all know! And just like casting this movie, I had this crazy curveball at the last minute where it was written for Mexico and we were going to shoot in the Dominican Republic. I was 10 days away from leaving and the studio calls me up and says, “Hey, some sound stages and a crew just became available in Bangkok. Can you shoot Thailand for Mexico?” And I was like, “Well, that’s bonkers. What are you guys talking about? That would be so challenging and I don’t really see the point.” And on top of that, I’m allergic to peanuts! I can’t go and spend six months in Thailand, I will probably die. I’m being serious, I go into anaphylactic shock, and they’re like, “We’ll get you a second assistant whose only job will be to feed you, make you dinner reservations, keep you alive and get your driver, in addition to your U.S. assistant!” I started thinking about the soccer team that got lost in the flooded cave system in Thailand, and how that was a part of our collective consciousness at the time and really in the zeitgeist. And I started doing some more research on freshwater cave systems in Thailand, and it started to feel a little bit more dangerous — a little bit more off the beaten path, a little bit more exotic, and I thought that would increase the credibility of what transpired. If it was just a system that tourists went to all the time in Mexico, for them to have gotten into this kind of trouble seemed a little less plausible. It also seemed like help would be there a lot sooner. But suddenly, you start setting it in a remote part of Thailand, it just feels further, more out the realm of these characters’ normal worlds. How did you approach filming the caves and meet the challenge of this one location? I wanted there to be this increasing sense of claustrophobia, so I started really wide and big. I wanted to make the trip look awesome and fun, and the location seem beautiful and appealing. I didn’t want the audience to ever go like, “Why are these people on this trip? This seems like a bad idea.” I wanted it to be obvious why they’re on the trip. It’s an amazing place to visit. Then I wanted to go into real caves that were mysterious and beautiful and not foreboding at all. I wanted the audience on the adventure, so I found real freshwater caves where rescue divers train. And then once they go around the corner, I went on a soundstage because shooting this movie in a real cave would be impossible. Forget just the lighting — the stunt work and safety issues would be massive. So once they’re in the cave system, we’re on a soundstage. We built a 120-foot long, 70-foot wide cave set and flooded it with five feet of water. We had one other set that was like 60-by-70 feet that had 15 feet of water. Between those two sets, I shot every cave. So we had 13 sets on two stages. It was just about turning them over and being really creative. Alec Hammond, my production designer, is just a mad scientist. We figured out how to shoot every square foot of every rock and make it look like it’s a different cave just by using lighting tricks and key set-pieces that we would turn or rotate. It was really difficult. There are multiple scenes where they swim off the set and they just swim back onto the same set. What were some of the biggest considerations for filming and lighting the underwater sequences? The lighting was really challenging because you want it to feel dark, but it can’t be darkness, right? We wanted to use the headlamps to motivate light, but you couldn’t really use them because if you tilted them down or got them anywhere near the lens, the lens would just flare out. We did a lot of experimentation with the headlamps. James Kniest, my director of photography, is also very good at his job. We ended up building these custom headlamps where we can control the luminance. But also we could angle them. And we would often yell from monitor like, “Hey, Lana, two clicks up!” And the cast knew that meant tilt it up, two clicks. And if you really study the movie, most of the time their headlamps are not pointed anywhere useful. But you see the light glowing, and in your mind it kind of motivates a general fill — that allowed us to come in with movie lights and get an exposure. I do think it works. I mean, if you study it, it falls apart pretty quickly. Ultimately, it was a digital system. It was much more about all the stuff that went around the cameras — the underwater housing, the HydroFlex, all those systems that we were using. That was another massive challenge with this film because I couldn’t use a dolly, couldn’t use a steadicam. I couldn’t even do handheld shots because when the camera is in water, even at water level, it has to be in the HydroFlex underwater housing. That weighs 120 pounds alone. You’re not doing a handheld shot, you got to use buoyancy to keep it up. I basically had to learn an entirely new cinematic language. I couldn’t use long lenses. I brought in Pete McCaffrey, who’s this legendary New Zealand camera operator, and he was just on the technocrane all day everyday. That was the only way I could really get the camera in and do some more traditional moves. But even those are impossible because you can’t drop marks in the water! How do the actors know where to go? In addition to getting to work with the local crew, what were some of the biggest benefits of filming in Thailand? As far as the actual economic incentives, the cost of living is much lower over there. We got a lot more bang for our buck. At a certain point, the cost of living can price a movie out of an area. If you’re having to pay a certain wage so people can live in that area, the studios only want to invest a certain amount of money in a movie. You can’t just physically make the movie there. And so sometimes, I thought a little bit about, “Alright, well we’re paying less than we would elsewhere. How do I feel about that?” And it was explained to me that this was a film industry hungry for projects. These were outstanding wages given the cost of living in that area and they were thrilled to have the work. So that’s how I wrapped my head around it. I really embraced Thailand as a character in the film and tried to make it feel like we couldn’t have shot the movie anywhere else. It wasn’t just about economic incentives or labor costs or equipment costs. The industry is really excited right now about the success of films like “Obsession” and “Backrooms” from younger directors. What do you make of these conversations happening in horror spaces? I mean, it’s just hard. It’s always going to be hard to get movies made. It’s not like Disney made “Obsession,” or Netflix made “Backrooms.” It’s not like major studios are embracing this kind of filmmaking. These are filmmakers that fought like hell to get their movies made, and I’m so happy that they’re enjoying this kind of success. I don’t think it’s going to make it any easier, though, to make movies. It might make it a little bit easier for Curry Barker to make his movie, obviously. But that’s the exception. That’s not the rule. I don’t think you’re going to see major studios chasing down young filmmakers who have had success with a couple YouTube shorts to make wide releases. Maybe I’m cynical, but I just don’t see that happening. I think it’s still going to be hard. It’s almost always going to be hard, and it’s hard for a reason because it tests you, and for that reason, only people who can really do it are able to keep doing it. “The Devil’s Mouth” is now streaming on Prime Video.
